findings.evidence: types.ts:64 OrderItem.price: number; types.ts:77 Order.total_amount: number; types.ts:78 Order.total?: number (alias). Backend PaginatedResponse (schemas.py:48-58) declares items: List[Any], total: int, page: int, size: int, pages: int. Frontend ListPage<T> (listResponse.ts:1-6) has data, total, page, pageSize — no pages field. normalizeListPage (listResponse.ts:8-36) maps items→data and size→pageSize but silently drops pages from the envelope.
findings.notes: Shape mismatch is real and current. Backend PaginatedResponse.pages (schemas.py:58) is silently lost in normalizeListPage. Monetary types (number vs backend Decimal) are standard JSON-serialization behavior and not a Law 19 violation on the frontend side. Finding is partially about type alignment (pages drop) and partially about monetary typing (acceptable on frontend).

findings.evidence: client.ts:38-44: resolveRequestUrl currently handles /auth/ (prepends /api/v1), absolute http(s) URLs (passes through), and all other paths starting with /api, /auth, or /admin (passes through). Paths starting with /cart/ fall through to the default return-path branch and are NOT remapped.
findings.counter_evidence: client.ts:42: paths starting with /admin are explicitly excluded from rewriting: 'if (!path.startsWith("/api") && !path.startsWith("/auth") && !path.startsWith("/admin")) return `/__api${path}`'. Admin API calls like /api/v1/admin/orders bypass resolveRequestUrl entirely (already absolute), so the /admin prefix gap cited in the finding is RESOLVED — admin paths are never rewritten, which is correct behavior. The remaining /cart/ gap is a separate unresolved issue not covered by this finding.
findings.notes: The finding's primary complaint — that /admin/ paths were unhandled — is RESOLVED: /admin/ is now explicitly excluded from rewriting in client.ts:42, and all current admin API calls use absolute /api/v1/admin/... paths.
